abolition.en: the act of officially ending something
abolition.ex: The abolition of the fee pleased many parents.

absorb.en: to take in and deal with a cost
absorb.ex: The company will absorb the extra costs.

according.ex: According to the report, prices fell last year.

account.en: a place where a bank keeps your money
account.ex: I opened a bank account today.

additional.ex: The school needs additional teachers next year.

address.en: to deal with a problem or need
address.ex: The new law will address the housing shortage.

advisory.ex: An advisory group will meet monthly.

agree.en: to have the same opinion; reach a deal
agree.ex: We need to agree on a plan.

all.en: every part; all told: in total

allocation.en: an amount of money given for a purpose
allocation.ex: Each school gets an allocation of funds.

example.en: Each class receives a small allocation for books.
example.zh: 每個班級都有一小筆買書的撥款。

note.meaning: 「撥款、分配額」，指被分配的一筆資金或資源。
note.usage: 可數名詞；常與 budget、funding 連用，如 budget allocation。

noteEn.meaning: An amount of money given for a purpose.

noteEs.exampleTr: Cada clase recibe una pequeña asignación para libros.
noteEs.meaning: Cantidad de dinero o recursos asignada a algo.

noteHi.exampleTr: हर कक्षा को किताबों के लिए थोड़ी राशि मिलती है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी उद्देश्य के लिए दी गई राशि; आवंटन।
noteHi.usage: गणनीय संज्ञा; budget allocation जैसे रूपों में।

noteJa.exampleTr: 各クラスには本のための少額の予算が配分される。
noteJa.meaning: 割り当てられた資金や資源、「配分（額）」。
noteJa.usage: 可算名詞。budget allocation の形でよく使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 각 반은 도서 구입을 위한 소액 예산을 받는다.
noteKo.usage: 셀 수 있는 명사로 budget allocation처럼 자주 쓴다.

also.ex: She speaks French and also Spanish.

alternative.en: different and able to replace another
alternative.ex: We need an alternative route home.

amount.en: amount to: reach a total of

announced.ex: The school announced a new head teacher.

apprised.ex: She apprised her boss of the problem.

appropriate.en: right or suitable for a situation
appropriate.ex: Wear appropriate shoes for the hike.

approval.ex: The plan needs approval from the council.

approximately.en: close to a number, not exact
approximately.ex: The trip takes approximately three hours.

as.en: in the same way; in the role of

asked.ex: She asked the council to fix the road.

at.en: in a place, time or level

back.en: to the place or state before

balance.en: the amount of money left in an account

bank.en: a money business; bank holiday: public holiday
bank.ex: Monday is a bank holiday in Ireland.

be.ex: Try to be on time tomorrow.

been.ex: It has been a busy week.

billion.ex: The project cost two billion euro.

borrow.en: take money that you will pay back
borrow.ex: Many students borrow money for college.

borrowing.ex: Borrowing is cheaper when interest rates are low.

briefed.ex: The officer briefed the team before the visit.

broader.ex: We need to look at the broader picture.

budget.ex: The school budget is very small this year.

budgetary.ex: There are budgetary limits this year.

buffer.en: something that protects against harm or shocks
buffer.ex: Savings act as a buffer against job loss.

cabinet.en: the group of top government ministers

capital.en: money used to start or run a business
capital.ex: They need capital to grow the firm.

channel.en: to send money in a particular direction

climate.en: the usual weather of an area over time

close.en: to shut; the end of a period
close.ex: The shop will close at six.

closing.ex: The shop is closing next month.

closure.en: the act of closing something for good
closure.ex: The closure of the factory hit the town hard.

coincides.en: happens at the same time as something else
coincides.ex: The festival coincides with the school holidays.

colleagues.ex: She had lunch with her colleagues.

commitment.en: a promise to give money or effort
commitment.ex: The city made a big commitment to new parks.

concluded.ex: The report concluded that money was wasted.

consequently.ex: It rained all day; consequently, the match was cancelled.

example.en: Costs rose; consequently, prices went up.
example.zh: 成本上升，因此價格上漲。

note.usage: 用於句首或分號後，表示因果；比 so 正式。

noteEn.usage: Use at the start of a sentence or after a semicolon.

noteEs.exampleTr: Los costes subieron; por consiguiente, los precios también.
noteEs.usage: Más formal que so; al inicio o tras punto y coma.

noteHi.usage: so से औपचारिक; वाक्य की शुरुआत या ; के बाद।

noteJa.exampleTr: 費用が上がり、その結果価格も上がった。
noteJa.usage: so より硬い。文頭やセミコロンの後で使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 비용이 올랐고, 그 결과 가격도 올랐다.

constitute.ex: These delays constitute a serious problem.

contingencies.en: possible events that are hard to predict
contingencies.ex: Plan for all contingencies before the trip.

contingency.en: a possible event that needs a plan; for emergencies
contingency.ex: We have a contingency plan for bad weather.

example.en: Every hospital needs a contingency plan.
example.zh: 每家醫院都需要一套應急計畫。

note.meaning: 應急；可能發生的意外情況。
note.usage: contingency fund/plan 指為意外準備的基金或計畫；複數 contingencies 指各種意外情況。

noteEn.meaning: a possible future event, often a problem, that you plan for.

noteEs.exampleTr: Todo hospital necesita un plan de contingencia.

noteHi.exampleTr: हर अस्पताल को आपात योजना चाहिए।
noteHi.usage: contingency fund/plan आपात निधि या योजना है।

noteJa.exampleTr: どの病院にも緊急時計画が必要だ。
noteJa.meaning: 不測の事態；緊急時の備え。
noteJa.usage: contingency fund/plan の形でよく使う。

contingent.ex: The trip is contingent on good weather.

contraction.en: a fall in the size of the economy
contraction.ex: The economy saw a sharp contraction.

contributions.ex: Workers make monthly contributions to the fund.

cost.ex: The cost of food keeps rising.

council.en: an official group that makes decisions

course.en: on course: likely to achieve something
course.ex: The team is on course to win the league.
course.zh: 進程（on course to：有望達到）

cover.en: to have enough money to pay for
cover.ex: The grant will cover the cost of books.

cumulatively.en: when all amounts are added together
cumulatively.ex: Cumulatively, the small fees became expensive.

current.ex: The current rules are too strict.

cushion.en: to reduce the bad effect of something
cushion.ex: Savings can cushion families against sudden costs.

dating.ex: It is a castle dating from the 1500s.

deal.en: deal with: to handle a problem
deal.ex: We must deal with the problem now.

decades.ex: The tree has grown for decades.

decision.ex: It was a hard decision to leave.

demographic.en: relating to the structure of a population
demographic.ex: Young adults are a key demographic.

designed.ex: The course is designed for beginners.

determined.ex: The fine will be determined later.

dormant.en: not active or used for a time
dormant.ex: The account lay dormant for ten years.

example.en: The seeds lay dormant until the spring rain.
example.zh: 種子一直休眠到春雨來臨。

note.meaning: 休眠的；暫時不活動但可能再活躍的。
note.usage: 用於火山、種子、計畫等；lie/remain dormant 為常見搭配，與 extinct 相對。

noteEn.meaning: Not active now, but able to become active again.
noteEn.usage: Common with volcanoes and seeds: lie dormant, remain dormant.

noteEs.exampleTr: Las semillas permanecieron latentes hasta la lluvia de primavera.
noteEs.meaning: Inactivo por ahora, pero puede volver a activarse.
noteEs.usage: Se usa con volcanes, semillas, planes; lie/remain dormant es común.

noteHi.exampleTr: बीज वसंत की बारिश तक सुप्त पड़े रहे।
noteHi.meaning: सुप्त; अभी निष्क्रिय पर बाद में सक्रिय हो सकता है।
noteHi.usage: ज्वालामुखी, बीज आदि के लिए; lie/remain dormant आम है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 種は春の雨まで休眠していた。
noteJa.meaning: 休眠中の、今は活動していないが再び活動しうる。
noteJa.usage: 火山・種子・計画などに使う。lie/remain dormant がよく使われる。

noteKo.exampleTr: 씨앗은 봄비가 올 때까지 휴면 상태였다.
noteKo.meaning: 휴면 상태의, 지금은 활동하지 않지만 다시 활동할 수 있는.
noteKo.usage: 화산, 씨앗, 계획 등에 쓰며 lie/remain dormant가 흔하다.

downturn.en: a period when the economy gets worse
downturn.ex: Many jobs were lost in the downturn.

downturns.en: periods when the economy gets worse

drawn.en: caused a reaction such as criticism
drawn.ex: The plan has drawn strong criticism.
drawn.zh: 招致；引來（批評）；動用（draw on）

during.en: at some time in a period

dwindled.ex: The crowd dwindled after the rain began.

early.ex: Early reports said nobody was hurt.

economic.en: related to money and the economy

end.en: the last part of a period
end.ex: We will finish by the end of May.

endowment.en: money given to set up a fund
endowment.ex: The school received a large endowment.

environmental.en: about nature and the natural world
environmental.ex: Plastic is a big environmental problem.

expected.ex: Snow is expected in the hills tonight.

extra.ex: We need extra chairs for the party.

far.ex: The level was far above the limit.

finance.zh: 財政（Minister for Finance：財政部長）

finances.en: the money a country or person has
finances.ex: The country's finances are in good shape.

example.en: The fiscal rules limit how much the State can borrow.
example.zh: 財政規則限制國家可借款的金額。

note.meaning: 財政的；與政府收支、稅收有關的。
note.usage: fiscal policy/year/council；與 financial 不同，fiscal 多指政府財政。

noteEn.meaning: about government money, taxes and spending.

noteEs.exampleTr: Las reglas fiscales limitan cuánto puede pedir prestado el Estado.
noteEs.usage: fiscal policy/year; se refiere al dinero del Estado.

noteHi.exampleTr: राजकोषीय नियम सरकारी उधार को सीमित करते हैं।
noteHi.usage: fiscal policy/year में प्रयोग; सरकार के धन से जुड़ा।

noteJa.exampleTr: 財政規則は国の借入額を制限する。
noteJa.meaning: 財政の（政府の収支に関する）。
noteJa.usage: fiscal policy/year など。主に政府の財政を指す。

noteKo.exampleTr: 재정 규칙은 국가 차입 규모를 제한한다.
noteKo.usage: fiscal policy/year 등; 주로 정부 재정을 말한다.

fledgling.ex: The fledgling company has five staff.

focus.en: the main thing that gets attention
focus.ex: The focus is now on saving money.

formative.en: important in shaping how something develops
formative.ex: Those were formative years for the young country.

fresh.ex: She was fresh from her holiday.

fund.en: money kept for a purpose; to pay for
fund.ex: A new fund will help small farms.

funds.ex: The charity raised funds for the hospital.

funnelled.en: sent money in a steady flow into something
funnelled.ex: Profits were funnelled into new projects.

further.ex: A further ten jobs will be created.

future.ex: Future students will benefit from the change.

government.en: the group of people who run a country
government.ex: The government will build new schools.

has.en: owns or holds; also forms perfect tense

have.ja: 持つ；〜しなければならない

help.ex: Volunteers help older people with shopping.

hit.ex: Prices hit a new high last month.

however.ex: It was sunny; however, it was cold.

implications.ex: The plan has big implications for jobs.

example.en: The new law has serious implications for small farms.
example.zh: 新法律對小型農場有重大影響。

note.usage: 常用複數 implications for sth；serious/far-reaching implications。

noteEn.meaning: a possible effect or result of something.

noteEs.exampleTr: La nueva ley tiene serias implicaciones para las pequeñas granjas.
noteEs.usage: Suele ir en plural: implications for sth; serious implications.

noteHi.exampleTr: नए क़ानून का छोटे खेतों पर गंभीर प्रभाव पड़ेगा।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर बहुवचन: implications for sth; serious implications।

noteJa.exampleTr: 新しい法律は小規模農場に深刻な影響を及ぼす。
noteJa.meaning: （将来の）影響；起こりうる結果。
noteJa.usage: 複数形 implications for ~ の形が多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 새 법은 소규모 농장에 심각한 영향을 미친다.
noteKo.meaning: 영향; 앞으로 생길 수 있는 결과.
noteKo.usage: 보통 복수형 implications for ~ 형태로 쓴다.

informed.ex: She informed the police about the crash.

infrastructure.en: basic systems like roads, power and water

initial.ex: My initial idea was to take a train.

injection.en: a large amount of money added at once
injection.ex: The cash injection saved the club.

intended.ex: The money is intended for schools.

investing.en: putting money into something to gain later
investing.ex: She is investing in a small business.

keep.ex: Keep trying and you will improve.

lain.en: stayed in a place or state (past of lie)
lain.ex: The old letters had lain in the box for years.
lain.zh: 閒置；躺（lie 的過去分詞，lain dormant：一直閒置）

larger.ex: They moved to a larger house.

latest.ex: Have you read her latest book?

latter.en: the second of two things just mentioned
latter.ex: Of the two plans, the latter is cheaper.

launched.en: started or made public for the first time
launched.ex: The new website was launched in May.
launched.ja: 発表された；開始された

leave.en: time away from work allowed by an employer
leave.ex: She is on sick leave this week.

managing.ex: She is good at managing money.

may.ex: Kids may start school at four.
may.ja: …かもしれない；…することがある

means.ex: Cycling is a cheap means of transport.

meant.ex: The money is meant to help families.

mechanisms.en: systems or ways of doing something
mechanisms.ex: The budget has new mechanisms for saving.

example.en: Scientists still study the mechanism behind memory.
example.zh: 科學家仍在研究記憶背後的機制。

note.usage: 學術上指造成某結果的過程，如 underlying mechanisms。

noteEn.meaning: the way something works or happens.

noteEs.exampleTr: Los científicos aún estudian el mecanismo de la memoria.
noteEs.usage: Proceso que causa un resultado: underlying mechanisms.

noteHi.exampleTr: वैज्ञानिक अब भी स्मृति के पीछे के तंत्र का अध्ययन करते हैं।
noteHi.usage: किसी परिणाम के पीछे की प्रक्रिया: underlying mechanisms।

noteJa.exampleTr: 科学者は今も記憶の仕組みを研究している。
noteJa.usage: 結果を生む過程。underlying mechanisms の形が多い。

meet.en: to pay for or deal with needs
meet.ex: They cannot meet the cost of repairs.

meeting.en: an event where people gather to talk

million.ex: The city has over one million people.

minister.en: a leader of a government department
minister.ex: The minister visited the new school.

ministers.ex: Ministers met to discuss the plan.

mitigate.en: to make something bad less serious
mitigate.ex: Trees can mitigate the effects of heat.

example.en: New walls will mitigate the risk of flooding.
example.zh: 新的堤牆將降低淹水風險。

note.usage: 受詞多為 impact、effects、risks、implications；不要和 militate 混淆。

noteEn.meaning: to make something bad less serious.

noteEs.exampleTr: Los nuevos muros mitigarán el riesgo de inundaciones.
noteEs.usage: Se usa con impact, effects, risks.

noteHi.exampleTr: नई दीवारें बाढ़ का ख़तरा कम करेंगी।
noteHi.usage: impact, effects, risks के साथ प्रयोग होता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 新しい壁が洪水のリスクを軽減する。

noteKo.exampleTr: 새 방벽이 홍수 위험을 줄일 것이다.

modest.ex: The town saw a modest rise in visitors.

money.ex: They saved money for a new car.

mounting.ex: There is mounting pressure on hospitals.

much.ex: The new phone is much faster.

nature.en: plants, animals and the natural world
nature.ex: We should protect nature for our children.

need.en: a situation where something is necessary
need.ex: There is a need for more teachers.

negligible.en: so small it is not important
negligible.ex: The cost of the change was negligible.

noteEn.meaning: so small that it is not important.

noteEs.usage: Contrario de significant; a negligible amount.

noteJa.exampleTr: 追加費用はごくわずかだ。

nevertheless.ex: It was raining; nevertheless, we went for a walk.

new.ex: She bought a new coat for winter.

next.ex: I will visit you next week.

not.ex: I do not like cold tea.

officials.ex: Officials met to discuss the plan.

old.en: having existed for a long time; of age

older.ex: My older brother lives in Galway.

on.en: touching a surface; on a day; about

onwards.en: starting from a time and continuing
onwards.ex: The shop is open from 9 a.m. onwards.

order.en: in order to: so that you can
order.ex: She studied hard in order to pass.

originally.ex: The house was originally a shop.

parallel.en: in parallel: at the same time
parallel.ex: The two tests ran in parallel.

paternity.en: being a father (paternity leave: time off for new fathers)
paternity.ex: He took two weeks of paternity leave.
paternity.ja: 父親であること（育児休暇）

pay.ex: The government will pay for the new hospital.

periods.ex: There were long periods of dry weather.

plans.ex: The town has plans for a new park.

point.ex: By that point, everyone was tired.

population.en: all the people living in a place
population.ex: The population of Dublin is growing.

projects.ex: The city has three big building projects.

protect.en: keep someone or something safe from harm
protect.ex: Sun cream helps protect your skin.

public.en: for or about everyone; in public: where others can see
public.ex: Public transport is cheap in the city.
public.zh: 公共的；（in public）在公共場合

put.ex: She put money into her savings.

rainy-day.en: kept for a future time of need
rainy-day.ex: We keep a rainy-day account for repairs.
rainy-day.zh: 應急的；以備不時之需的（rainy-day fund）

raises.en: causes a question to be asked

reach.en: to get to a certain level
reach.ex: Prices could reach a new high.

recommended.en: suggested as the best thing to do

reflects.en: shows or is caused by something

relative.ex: Prices are high relative to wages.

relic.en: something old that survives from the past
relic.ex: The old phone box is a relic of the past.

remained.ex: The shop remained open all night.

remaining.ex: With nine days remaining, the race is open.

reserves.ex: The bank holds large cash reserves.

residual.en: left over after the main part is gone
residual.ex: The residual money was given to charity.

retired.ex: The old train will be retired next year.

returned.ex: The money will be returned to the bank.

revert.en: to go back to a former owner or state
revert.ex: The land will revert to the council.

safeguard.ex: The law is a safeguard for workers.

sanction.ex: The board must sanction the spending.

sat.en: stayed in a place or state
sat.ex: The money sat in the bank for years.

saving.ex: He is saving for a new car.

savings.en: money that is kept for later
savings.ex: She keeps her savings in a bank.

say.ex: Gardaí say more people died this year.

says.ex: Experts say the plan will work.

second.ex: This is my second visit to Paris.

serving.en: acting as or being used as
serving.ex: The room is serving as an office.
serving.hi: के रूप में काम करते हुए

set.en: set up: start; set out: explain clearly
set.ex: The club was set up in 1980.

shifts.en: moves something to a different place or aim
shifts.ex: The firm shifts its focus to online sales.

sister.en: of the same type and closely linked
sister.ex: The hotel has a sister hotel in Cork.

sought.en: asked for or tried to get
sought.ex: She sought advice from a lawyer.

source.en: a place where something comes from
source.ex: Fish is a good source of protein.

sovereign.ex: The country set up a sovereign wealth fund.
sovereign.zh: 主權的；國家的（sovereign savings：國家儲蓄）

specifically.ex: The tool is designed specifically for students.

state.ex: The State pays for public schools.

state's.ex: The State's lawyers lost the case.

strains.ex: Rising prices put strains on families.

strategy.en: a plan to reach a long-term goal
strategy.ex: We need a clear strategy to save money.

substantial.ex: The new road needs a substantial amount of money.

example.en: The town received a substantial grant.
example.zh: 小鎮獲得一筆可觀的補助。

note.usage: IELTS 常用來取代 big/large；a substantial increase/sum。

noteEs.exampleTr: El pueblo recibió una subvención considerable.
noteEs.usage: Sustituye a big/large; a substantial sum.

noteHi.exampleTr: शहर को एक बड़ा अनुदान मिला।
noteHi.usage: big/large के स्थान पर; a substantial sum/increase।

noteJa.exampleTr: 町は多額の補助金を受けた。
noteJa.usage: big/large の言い換え。a substantial increase。

such.en: of this kind; such as: for example

sudden.ex: A sudden storm closed the roads.

suited.en: right or good for a purpose
suited.ex: This car is well suited to city driving.

sum.ex: They paid a large sum for the house.

support.en: to agree with and help; to keep going

sustainability.en: using resources without harming the future

example.en: The school teaches pupils about sustainability.
example.zh: 這所學校教學生永續發展的觀念。

noteEn.meaning: using resources in a way that protects the future.

noteEs.exampleTr: La escuela enseña a los alumnos sobre sostenibilidad.

noteHi.exampleTr: स्कूल बच्चों को स्थिरता के बारे में सिखाता है।
noteHi.meaning: स्थिरता; पर्यावरण की रक्षा करते हुए विकास।

noteJa.exampleTr: その学校は生徒に持続可能性について教えている。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 학교는 학생들에게 지속 가능성에 대해 가르친다.

taken.ex: No money has been taken from the box.

tapped.ex: The fund has not been tapped in years.

there.ex: We went to the park and played there.

these.en: the ones here or just mentioned

time.ex: For the first time, dentists will join.

today.ex: Today there are fewer than 70 growers.

told.en: said to someone; all told: in total

transfer.en: moving something from one owner to another
transfer.ex: The transfer of the company took six months.

transfers.en: movements of money from one place to another
transfers.ex: Transfers to the fund began in 2024.

transition.en: the change from one state to another
transition.ex: The transition to electric cars will take years.

unexpected.ex: We had an unexpected visitor today.

unforeseen.ex: Unforeseen delays pushed back the opening.

example.en: The trip was cancelled due to unforeseen circumstances.
example.zh: 由於不可預見的情況，旅行被取消了。

paragraphs: Ireland has a very old fund for emergencies. The Government now plans to close it.
The fund started in 1923. That was in the first years of the Irish state. It began with £20,000.
Nobody has used the money for 22 years. Only €1.2 million is left in it. The money will go back to the State.
Jack Chambers is the minister for public spending. He told the Cabinet about the plan on Wednesday.
Finance Minister Simon Harris also has a plan. He wants to put €1 billion into a different fund next year. This fund will help pay for older people in the future.
By the end of 2027, it should have about €22.8 billion. But a State money watchdog says the Government may need to borrow to keep saving.
sentZh: 愛爾蘭有一個非常古老的緊急基金。
政府現在計畫關閉它。
這個基金始於1923年。
那是愛爾蘭建國初期。
它最初有兩萬英鎊。
22年來沒有人動用過這筆錢。
基金裡只剩下120萬歐元。
這筆錢將回到國家手中。
傑克·錢伯斯是負責公共支出的部長。
他在週三向內閣說明了這項計畫。
財政部長賽門·哈里斯也有一項計畫。
他希望明年把10億歐元投入另一個基金。
這個基金將幫助支付未來高齡人口的開銷。
到2027年底，這個基金應有約228億歐元。
但國家的財政監督機構表示，政府可能需要借錢才能持續儲蓄。

paragraphs: The Government is closing a savings fund that is more than 100 years old. The fund was created to pay for sudden emergencies, but it has not been used for a long time.
The contingency fund was set up in 1923, in the early years of the Irish state. It started with £20,000 to cover costs that nobody could plan for.
However, no one has taken money from it for 22 years. Today it holds about €1.2 million. Officials say there are now better ways in the budget to deal with unexpected costs.

Jack Chambers, the Minister for Public Expenditure, updated other ministers about the plan at the Cabinet meeting on Wednesday. The money that is left will go back to the Exchequer, the State's main bank account.
At the same meeting, Finance Minister Simon Harris asked the Cabinet to agree to put an extra €1 billion into the Future Ireland Fund next year. He is back at work this week after paternity leave.
The Future Ireland Fund was set up in 2024. It will help the State pay for an ageing population from 2041 onwards. With the new money, it should reach about €22.8 billion by the end of 2027.

A second fund, for infrastructure, climate and nature, should reach €8 billion. However, the State's budget watchdog warned earlier this year that the Government may need to borrow money to keep paying into these funds.
sentZh: 政府正在關閉一個已有一百多年歷史的儲蓄基金。
這個基金是為了支付突發緊急事件而設立的，但已經很久沒有被使用。
這個應急基金於1923年設立，當時是愛爾蘭建國初期。
它最初有兩萬英鎊，用來支付無法事先規劃的費用。
然而，22年來沒有人從中提取過錢。
如今基金裡約有120萬歐元。
官員表示，現在預算中已有更好的方式處理意外支出。
公共支出部長傑克·錢伯斯在週三的內閣會議上向其他部長說明了這項計畫。
剩下的錢將回到國庫，也就是國家的主要銀行帳戶。
在同一場會議上，財政部長賽門·哈里斯請內閣同意明年再投入10億歐元到「未來愛爾蘭基金」。
他休完陪產假，本週回到工作崗位。
「未來愛爾蘭基金」於2024年設立。
它將幫助國家支付2041年起高齡化人口的開銷。
加上這筆新資金，到2027年底基金應可達約228億歐元。
另一個用於基礎設施、氣候與自然的基金應可達到80億歐元。
不過，國家的預算監督機構今年稍早警告，政府可能需要借錢才能持續注資這些基金。

paragraphs: The Government is to wind up a 103-year-old emergency fund that has sat untouched for more than two decades, as it shifts its focus to much larger long-term savings funds.

The contingency fund was established in 1923, during the early years of the Irish state, with an initial £20,000 to cover unforeseen emergencies. It has not been drawn on in 22 years and now holds a balance of about €1.2 million.

Minister for Public Expenditure Jack Chambers briefed Cabinet colleagues on the plan on Wednesday. Officials recommended that other budget mechanisms should be used for contingency funding instead, and the remaining balance will be returned to the Exchequer.
Meanwhile, Minister for Finance Simon Harris, who returned to work this week after paternity leave, sought approval to transfer an additional €1 billion into the Future Ireland Fund next year.

The fund was created in 2024 to help the State meet the rising costs of an ageing population and other demographic pressures from 2041 onwards. Following the latest transfer, it is expected to be worth €22.77 billion by the end of 2027.

A second fund, the Infrastructure, Climate and Nature Fund, is projected to reach €8 billion by the same point. It is designed to protect public investment during an economic downturn and to support environmental projects.

Together, the two funds will have received more than €30 billion by the end of 2027. Earlier this year, however, the Irish Fiscal Advisory Council warned that the State may have to borrow in order to keep investing in them.
sentZh: 政府將結束一個已有103年歷史、二十多年未動用的緊急基金，同時把重心轉向規模大得多的長期儲蓄基金。
這個應急基金於1923年愛爾蘭建國初期設立，最初有兩萬英鎊，用於支付不可預見的緊急事件。
它已22年未被動用，目前餘額約為120萬歐元。
公共支出部長傑克·錢伯斯週三向內閣同僚簡報了這項計畫。
官員建議改用其他預算機制來提供應急資金，剩餘款項將歸還國庫。
與此同時，本週休完陪產假復工的財政部長賽門·哈里斯尋求批准，明年再撥10億歐元進入「未來愛爾蘭基金」。
該基金於2024年設立，旨在幫助國家應對2041年起高齡化人口及其他人口結構壓力所帶來的成本上升。
在最新一筆撥款之後，預計到2027年底其價值將達227.7億歐元。
第二個基金「基礎設施、氣候與自然基金」預計到同一時間將達80億歐元。
它的設計目的是在經濟衰退時保護公共投資，並支持環境項目。
到2027年底，這兩個基金合計將獲得超過300億歐元。
不過，愛爾蘭財政諮詢委員會今年稍早警告，國家可能必須借款才能持續投資這些基金。

paragraphs: A relic of the fledgling Irish state is to be quietly retired: the Government is winding up a 103-year-old rainy-day fund that has lain dormant for more than two decades.

Established in 1923 with an initial endowment of £20,000, the contingency fund was intended to absorb the cost of unforeseen emergencies. Yet it has not been tapped for 22 years, and its balance has dwindled to a modest €1.2 million.

Minister for Public Expenditure Jack Chambers apprised his Cabinet colleagues of the decision on Wednesday. Officials concluded that alternative budgetary mechanisms are better suited to contingency funding, and the residual sum will revert to the Exchequer.

The closure coincides with a far more substantial commitment. Minister for Finance Simon Harris, fresh from paternity leave, sought Cabinet sanction to channel a further €1 billion into the Future Ireland Fund next year.

Launched in 2024, that fund is meant to cushion the State against the mounting costs of an ageing population and other demographic strains from 2041 onwards. The latest injection should swell its value to €22.77 billion by the end of 2027.
Its sister vehicle, the Infrastructure, Climate and Nature Fund, is on course to hit €8 billion, serving both as a buffer against downturns and as a source of green investment.

All told, more than €30 billion will have been funnelled into the two funds by the close of 2027, although the Irish Fiscal Advisory Council cautioned earlier this year that sustaining such contributions may ultimately require borrowing.
sentZh: 愛爾蘭建國初期的一項遺物即將悄悄退場：政府正在結束一個已閒置二十多年、擁有103年歷史的「雨天基金」。
這個應急基金於1923年以兩萬英鎊的初始資本設立，原意是承擔不可預見的緊急開支。
然而它已22年未被動用，餘額也縮減到區區120萬歐元。
公共支出部長傑克·錢伯斯週三向內閣同僚通報了這項決定。
官員認為其他預算機制更適合用來提供應急資金，剩餘款項將歸還國庫。
這次關閉恰逢一項規模大得多的資金承諾。
剛結束陪產假的財政部長賽門·哈里斯尋求內閣批准，明年再向「未來愛爾蘭基金」注入10億歐元。
該基金於2024年推出，旨在緩衝2041年起高齡化人口及其他人口結構壓力帶來的日益增加的成本。
最新一筆注資應能使其價值在2027年底膨脹至227.7億歐元。
其姊妹基金「基礎設施、氣候與自然基金」有望達到80億歐元，既是抵禦經濟衰退的緩衝，也是綠色投資的資金來源。
總計到2027年底，將有超過300億歐元流入這兩個基金，不過愛爾蘭財政諮詢委員會今年稍早警告，要維持這樣的注資最終可能需要借款。

paragraphs: The Government has announced the abolition of a contingency fund dating from 1923, a decision that reflects a broader transition from small-scale emergency reserves towards substantial, long-term sovereign savings.

The fund was originally established with £20,000 to address unforeseen expenditure in the formative years of the State. Nevertheless, it has remained unused for 22 years, and its current balance of approximately €1.2 million is negligible relative to contemporary public finances.

According to Minister for Public Expenditure Jack Chambers, who informed the Cabinet on Wednesday, officials have determined that alternative budgetary mechanisms constitute a more appropriate means of managing contingencies. Consequently, the remaining balance will be returned to the Exchequer.

In parallel, Minister for Finance Simon Harris sought approval for an additional €1 billion allocation to the Future Ireland Fund in 2027. This fund was established in 2024 specifically to mitigate the fiscal implications of an ageing population from 2041 onwards.

Following this allocation, the fund is projected to amount to €22.77 billion by the end of 2027, while the Infrastructure, Climate and Nature Fund is expected to reach €8 billion. The latter is intended to safeguard capital investment during periods of economic contraction.

Cumulatively, transfers to the two funds will exceed €30 billion. However, the Irish Fiscal Advisory Council has warned that continued contributions may be contingent upon government borrowing, which raises questions about the long-term sustainability of the strategy.
sentZh: 政府宣布廢除一個始於1923年的應急基金，這項決定反映出從小規模緊急儲備轉向大規模、長期國家儲蓄的更廣泛轉變。
該基金最初以兩萬英鎊設立，用於應對國家形成時期的不可預見支出。
儘管如此，它已22年未被使用，目前約120萬歐元的餘額相對於當代公共財政而言微不足道。
據週三向內閣通報的公共支出部長傑克·錢伯斯表示，官員已確定其他預算機制是管理應急情況更合適的方式。
因此，剩餘款項將歸還國庫。
與此同時，財政部長賽門·哈里斯尋求批准，在2027年向「未來愛爾蘭基金」額外撥款10億歐元。
該基金於2024年設立，專門用來減輕2041年起人口高齡化帶來的財政影響。
在這筆撥款之後，預計到2027年底該基金將達227.7億歐元，而「基礎設施、氣候與自然基金」預計將達80億歐元。
後者旨在經濟萎縮期間保障資本投資。
累計而言，撥入這兩個基金的款項將超過300億歐元。
然而，愛爾蘭財政諮詢委員會警告，持續注資可能取決於政府借款，這引發了外界對該策略長期可持續性的疑問。
